diagnosis.summary: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the 10:15 deployment. The issue is likely due to the database connection pool being exhausted.
diagnosis.root_cause: The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the database connection pool size to 10, leading to connection pool exhaustion in production.

evidence.finding: Production p95 latency is 2150 ms, breaching the SLO of 400 ms.
Connection pool is fully utilized (in_use: 10, max_connections: 10) with 143 waiting connections.
The commit a91f3c2 removed database pool settings and set max_connections to 10.
Staging p95 latency is 180 ms with no connection pool issues.
Staging connection pool is not exhausted (in_use: 5, max_connections: 50).
All pods are running and healthy with version v4.17.
The migration to orders-client v3 is the likely cause of the connection pool issue.
Production acquire_wait_p95_ms is 1800 ms, indicating connection pool exhaustion.

ruled_out: The staging environment does not show the same latency or connection pool issues, ruling out a code change issue.
The pods are healthy and running the same version in production, ruling out pod health or version mismatch.

proposal.rationale: The Checkout API's p95 latency increased to 2150 ms in production after the deployment of version v4.17, which is likely due to the database connection pool being exhausted. The migration to orders-client v3 reduced the connection pool size to 10, leading to the issue. Rolling back to the previous version, v4.16, will restore the connection pool settings and resolve the latency issue.
